en: Points of Controversy,
Great Chapter Five,
Ninth Section
The Discussion on Whether Knowledge is Without an Object.
Is knowledge without an object?
Yes, it is.
Is form Nibbāna? Is the eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base Nibbāna?
One should not say so …pe…
Is knowledge without an object? Yes.
Then is wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view, and the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment without an object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is wisdom,
the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view, the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment, with an object? Yes.
“Knowledge has an object”?
One should not say so… [and so on] … “Knowledge has no object”? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“To which aggregate does it belong?
“It belongs to the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha).”
Is the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) without an object (anārammaṇa)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object?
[The opponent says: “Yes.
[The proponent asks: “Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of consciousness without an object?
[The opponent replies: “One should not say so…” [and so on].
Is knowledge included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and without an object? Yes.
Is wisdom (paññā) included in the aggregate of mental formations and without an object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is wisdom included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and does it have an object? Yes.
Is knowledge included in the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) and with an object (sārammaṇa)?

One should not say so… [as before] … Is knowledge included in the aggregate of mental formations and without an object (anārammaṇa), while wisdom (paññā) included in the aggregate of mental formations is with an object?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is it to be said that one part of the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) has an object (sārammaṇa) and another part has no object (anārammaṇa)?
You must not say so …pe…
Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha) has an object and another part is without an object?
Yes.

Is it the case that one part of the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha), the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha), and the aggregate of consciousness (viññāṇakkhandha) has an object and another part is without an object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “knowledge is without an object”?
“Yes.
“Then it must be said that an Arahant who possesses eye-consciousness is a possessor of knowledge?
“Yes.”
Is there an object for that knowledge?
You must not say so...
[and so on] ...therefore, knowledge is indeed without an object.
Should it be said that an Arahant who possesses eye-consciousness is possessed of wisdom?
Yes. Is there an object for that wisdom?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Therefore, wisdom has no object.
The discussion on whether knowledge has no object is concluded.
